items.response:
Morning. I don't see a new text or email from Nate yet, so nothing has landed since his Barzotti call. The last schedule I have from him had the kitchen renovation finishing by August 28, 2026, so I'll flag it if the new one moves that.
Action: Check your texts and email for anything from Nate and tell you as soon as it arrives, comparing it to the August 28 finish date.

Sweet of you, and he'll need it with interviews until 8. I don't know how Sam takes his coffee or whether he wants anything specific to snack on, and I'd rather not guess for a long evening like that.
Action: Look for a cafe that can deliver to Riverdale for about 3:30 (room 214, and I'll check if it has to go via the front office), then send you the order to confirm his coffee and snack before I place it.

I haven't opened the saved Kanchi Silks House link yet, so I don't have the price and I won't guess at it. Once I have it I'll show it in CAD with the rupee price in brackets, using the 1 CAD = 63.4 INR rate I have (dated 2025-11-01, so I'll check it's still current). For whether it's tourist pricing, I'll compare it with similar sarees from other sellers.
Action: Open the link, pull the price and the weave or fabric details, convert to CAD, and compare against a few similar sarees to tell you if it's reasonable.

Added, with you as owner. On the weekend: that is six stops on Saturday, and you like one main activity a day with a quiet afternoon break since Leo melts down when it's too full, so I'd make Sandbanks the main thing and keep one winery plus the cheese shop, moving the rest to Sunday. Also, your call with your mom is Saturdays at 8:30, which falls right after the 8:00 departure (Sam's driving, so you could take it in the car, or we could shift it), and Leo's swim lesson is at 10:00 if he's coming along.
Action: Add the action item, then draft a lighter Saturday and an easy Sunday for you to react to, and ask whether Leo is coming and how you want to handle the 8:30 call.

Here's a short version you can send her. Pros: better retention and morale, often steady or better output because people focus more, and a real hiring edge. Cons: client coverage and meeting scheduling get harder, workload can just get compressed into four longer days, and it needs clear rules on who covers what. I don't know her firm's size or kind of work, which changes the weighting.
Action: Put this into a short message for you to forward, and ask you what kind of firm it is so I can tailor the cons.

Sorry for Hannah, that's a rough one. The usual path is to find out which impound lot the car went to, then she shows ID, proof of ownership and insurance, and pays the tow, any ticket and storage, which can build daily so sooner is cheaper. I don't want to quote amounts without checking, since fees vary.
Action: Look up how to locate a car towed from Logan Ave and the current tow and storage fees, and send you a short step-by-step for Hannah, including checking whether the street-cleaning sign was actually posted.

Here's a draft for Hannah: 'Hi Hannah, thank you so much for taking Biscuit tomorrow morning! We're leaving at 5 and the cottage doesn't allow dogs. He's usually walked around 6:30 am, and he's a beagle, so please keep him leashed and keep bread and food off the counters because he's very food-motivated. Breakfast is [amount and where it is], and I'll leave a key and my number.' On sirens, beagles are hounds bred to howl, and a fire truck or ambulance sounds like another dog howling, so he joins in. It's instinct, not distress, and you asked about this after he howled at an ambulance in July 2025.
Action: Check what day tomorrow is so I put the right walk route in, ask you for his feeding amount, then send the text to Hannah once you OK it.

Happy to help with both, and getting ahead of the anniversary is a good idea. I don't have a note on what he's into lately or the exact dates, so I'll start from your calendar and past gift notes and not guess. A quick tell: what has he mentioned wanting this year, and do you want the birthday to be low-key or a bigger night out?
Action: Check your calendar for the dates of his birthday and your anniversary, pull any gift notes or past celebrations, and come back with 3 gift ideas, 2 celebration plans, and a reminder two weeks before the anniversary.

Good idea, a Zoom link will be less stressful for her than WhatsApp video. Your weekly call is Saturdays at 8:30 am Toronto time, which is 6:00 pm in Mumbai, so I'll put both times on the invite and in the text. I'll keep the message to your mom short and clear, with one tap to join.
Action: Create the Zoom for this Saturday at 8:30 am Toronto (6:00 pm IST), and text the link and times to your mom.

I'm sorry about Sam's migraine, and I won't say anything to Grace. For a thank-you with no scent, I'd go with something to share or use: good chocolates or baked goods from a local shop, a nice cheese and cracker set, or a hardcover cookbook or coffee-table book. I'd steer clear of flowers and anything perfumed.
Action: Look up a few shops near the Glebe that are open tomorrow (checking holiday hours), shortlist three non-scented options you can pick up, and send them to you.

Fun plan. Since you like one main activity a day with a quiet break after, I'll look for a pumpkin patch that's the whole outing, not a stop on a bigger itinerary. I'll aim for a smaller farm that isn't a theme-park scale zoo, within 45 minutes of home.
Action: Search pumpkin patches within 45 minutes, check today's hours, crowd levels and reviews, and send you two or three picks that fit a 1:30 departure.

Dinosaur it is. I'll look at Canadian retailers first, like MEC, Indigo and Simons, and only go to Amazon if nothing local can deliver before Friday 30 Jan. I'll keep it under $50 in a size 7.
Action: Search Canadian retailers for a dinosaur costume in size 7 under $50 that arrives in time, then order the best match, or send you options if nothing fits the date or budget.

Congrats to the team on beta wrapping up. For a group of eight on a Thursday, I'll look for places that take reservations for larger tables and have options for different diets. I'll use the office address from your calendar to keep it walkable.
Action: Find three or four spots near the office that can seat 8 next Thursday, check availability and menus, and send you the shortlist with reservation times before I book anything.

Here's what I can say from this chat so far: I've drafted the data request for Wen, saved your Vancouver flight preferences, added your Saturday run to the calendar, confirmed internet is Bell Fibe at $95 a month, and started the payouts v2 PRD skeleton in Notion. I don't yet have a clean list of your automatic monthly payments or the status of the Amazon batteries order, so I won't guess on either.
Action: Pull your recurring pre-authorized payments from the bank statements, check the Amazon order status for the batteries, and put together a fuller history of what I've done for you.

I don't have the VIA Rail results from 2026-02-27 in front of me, and I'd rather not reconstruct times from memory and risk giving you wrong ones. I'll look for that conversation first.
Action: Search my history and your notes for the 2026-02-27 VIA search; if I can't find it, I'll run a fresh Toronto to Ottawa Friday evening search and give you times and fares to compare with driving.

Got it, short replies today.
Action: I'll keep everything to a line or two and hold anything non-urgent until after 5.

I'm thinking of you, and of your dad. Tomorrow is a Wednesday, which usually has your 9:45 standup, your 1:1 with Tom at 11:30, and school pickup for Leo and Jun, so I'll see what's actually there and what can move. I won't decline or reschedule anything until you've okayed it.
Action: Pull up tomorrow's calendar, propose what to skip, move or make async (starting with the Tom 1:1 and standup), flag the pickup so you can decide whether to swap with Hannah, and keep your evening clear for the diya.

Leo was born July 17, 2019, so he's a child applicant and a parent applies for him. I don't want to give you a checklist from memory that could be out of date, so I'll build it from the official Government of Canada page: the child application form, his current passport, new passport photos, and parent ID are what I expect, plus any extra documents the page requires. With a January expiry, it's worth starting soon.
Action: Pull the official child-renewal checklist and fees, then find the nearest passport service locations with available appointments and send you the options.

A board-game do-over for an anniversary that came with a recital sounds lovely, and a Saturday works around Sam's Sunday marking. I'd look at a board-game cafe or a restaurant night with a game afterwards. I'll avoid Sundays and check which Saturdays Leo's schedule is clear.
Action: Check your calendar for open Saturdays over the next few weeks and shortlist a few board-game cafes or dinner-and-games options, then send you dates and places to pick from.

For the form: Biscuit is a beagle born around April 2022, so I'll write 'approx. April 2022' unless you have an exact date in his adoption paperwork. For behavioural notes: very food-motivated, steals bread off the counter, and howls at sirens (a typical beagle trait). It's also worth noting that chicken-based food gave him itchy skin, and he eats Purina Pro Plan Sensitive Skin & Stomach (salmon).
Action: Check for an exact birth date in your records and write the notes into the intake form for you to review.

Got it, I'll keep replies short.
Action: Short answers from here on, and anything that can wait will be saved for after 5.

On it, all tentative. I'll block Mon 15 and Tue 16 March for prep, Wed 17 and Thu 18 March for the offsite, and put 'roadmap deck due' on Fri 12 March.
Action: Check those days for clashes first, then create the tentative events and tell you if anything conflicts.

Short version for Leo: poppies grew on the battlefields of Flanders in WWI, because they bloom in churned-up soil. A Canadian doctor, John McCrae, wrote the poem 'In Flanders Fields' in 1915, and it made the poppy the symbol of remembering soldiers who died. People started wearing them in the early 1920s, and the Royal Canadian Legion hands them out, with donations helping veterans.
Action: I can turn that into a two-sentence kid version for Leo if you want it.

How lovely that Priya is visiting. Since she's on a mystery kick, a hardcover from a favourite author of yours like Tana French could be a good pick, though I'd check what she already has. Here's a card: 'Priya, I'm so happy you're coming. Here's a mystery for your kick, and I want your theories over coffee. Love, Riya.'
Action: Search Indigo for a hardcover mystery in stock that can arrive before next weekend, send you two options with prices, and keep the card text ready to print or write.

That sounds perfect, you've earned it. Nothing needs a response before Monday, so I'll keep Slack and work quiet.
Action: Stay quiet today and bring up the drop-off errands and anything else on Monday.

Partly. Portuguese and Spanish share a lot of vocabulary and grammar, so reading signs and menus will be much easier with your Spanish, but spoken Portuguese sounds quite different, and Spanish speakers often find it hard to follow at first. For Lisbon, you'll get by better with a few Portuguese basics, and many people there speak English.
Action: Put together a one-page list of the key Portuguese phrases and a few Spanish-to-Portuguese false friends for the Lisbon trip.

That is a fantastic career plan, and Sam's question deserves the 'obviously.' A paleontologist who makes dino-shaped pizzas feels very on brand for Leo.
Action: Save that quote to your notes so you have it later.

On it. I'll keep the checklist to 15 items, with fragrance-free cleaning products because of Sam's migraines, and include a check of the sump pump and basement back wall before heavy spring rain, swapping the furnace filter (16x25x1), and easing the sticking upstairs bathroom door. For the couch, I'll compare a haul-away service against city bulk pickup.
Action: Save the checklist to Notes and send you three couch removal options with prices and earliest dates, without booking until you confirm.

I can fill both from what I have. Your half marathon PB is 2:04:37 from the Toronto Waterfront Half Marathon on October 19, 2025, which is the only half on record for you, so tell me if you've run a faster one since. Property tax is paid in instalments by pre-authorized debit from the TD joint account.
Action: Fill in both boxes as drafts for you to review, and I won't submit the mortgage form myself.

I can draft that, but I can't give Olivia a date since Aisha hasn't signed off on one, so I'll use 'target' wording. Here's a draft: 'Hi Olivia, thanks for the heads up on Monday's call. Instant payouts is still limited to beta merchants, and I can't commit to a date until Aisha has signed off. I'll share a target as soon as we have one. Best, Riya'
Action: Pull the latest instant payouts status from Linear and Notion, check with Aisha on whether she can sign off on a target before Monday, and keep the draft ready for your review, unsent.

Sure, I'll read Carlos's email and give you a straight take on whether it's worth it or overkill. I'll weigh the cost, the added time and how it fits your Spanish goals.
Action: Open Carlos's email, summarize the price, schedule and deadline, and send you a recommendation.

Understood on the pet budget, it's $729 a month against $350 now, so that's a good one to raise with Sam. For the launch risks, I'll pull the open ones from Linear and set the Notion doc up for tomorrow's standup.
Action: Pull every open Payouts launch risk from Linear into one Notion doc with owner, due date, status, mitigation and next step for each, and send you the link.

Sending the text to Rui now. For the Chos, Saturday the 14th is Valentine's Day, so I'd book early. Saffron Lane on Queen Street East is a strong candidate since you love South Indian food and it should have plenty for Sam, who is vegetarian and doesn't eat fish or seafood.
Action: Send Rui the text, then check tables for 4 at 19:00 on Sat 14 Feb at Saffron Lane and a couple of backups in Leslieville or Riverside with good vegetarian options, and ask whether the Chos have any dietary needs.

That sounds stressful, and it makes sense you're spinning, but a missed call and a dead phone is the most likely explanation. Let's make a plan instead of waiting: try her again at a time she's likely up, and check her WhatsApp last seen. If there's still no answer by this evening, we ask a neighbour or relative near her in Bandra to check on her.
Action: Pull up the contacts for anyone who lives near your mom, set a reminder to retry her at an hour that suits Mumbai time, and draft a short text to her for you to send.

Morning. I don't see anything new from Nate yet, so I can't tell you what the schedule says. I'd rather check than guess.
Action: Check your texts and email for a message from Nate and let you know as soon as I find it.

I'll pull October's grocery spend from the TD statement, then the same for August and September so the comparison is like for like. Your household bills run through the joint chequing with Sam, so I'll check that account and any card used at grocery stores.
Action: Total October grocery transactions from TD, do the same for August and September, and send you the three numbers with the difference.

I'm thinking of you today, and your dad. I'll go through tomorrow and see what can move, and I won't decline or change anything until you say so. Your evening stays clear for the diya.
Action: Pull up tomorrow's calendar, propose what to move, decline or make async, and send it to you to approve.

Happy long weekend! Here's a checklist, ordered so the first step helps the rest:
- [ ] Find the good extension cord
- [ ] Sort the garage recycling
- [ ] Fix Leo's bike chain
- [ ] Hang the hallway mirror
- [ ] Plant the tomato seedlings
Action: Save it to your notes as today's list.

I can't fill these in yet, since I don't have your half marathon time or race on record and I'd rather not guess. The same goes for how property tax is handled on the mortgage form. I'll check your records first.
Action: Search your email, notes and any running app for race results, and check bank statements for how property tax is paid, then fill both in as drafts for you to confirm. If you remember either, tell me.

Here's one for Ellie: 'Biscuit is a beagle, and beagles were bred to sing to each other when they were hunting. When he hears the fire truck, it sounds to him like another dog singing, so he sings back.' It's his instinct and he isn't scared. You also asked me for an article summary on why beagles howl back in August 2025, so I can send it if you want more detail.
Action: Turn that into a short kid-friendly version you can tell Ellie tomorrow.

Happy to find it. I'll look for fully refundable rates under $250 a night in or near the Plateau, ideally walkable to the metro. Because this would be over $200, I'll send you my top pick for a quick yes before I book.
Action: Search refundable hotels for Fri 6 to Sun 8 Feb near the Plateau, pick the best one, and send it to you for confirmation, then book it right away.

Here are the approximate gram weights: flour 1 1/2 cups is about 190 g, sugar 1 cup about 200 g, butter 1/2 cup about 113 g, plain yogurt 1/2 cup about 125 g, lemon juice 2 tbsp about 30 g, and baking powder 1 tsp about 4 g. Flour varies with how you scoop it, so I used about 125 g per cup.
Action: Save this converted list to your notes with the recipe.

A hardcover mystery is a lovely idea. Since you love Tana French, one of her novels could work, but I'd check Priya doesn't already own it. Card: 'Priya, I'm so glad you're coming. Here's a mystery for your kick, and I want your theories over coffee. Love, Riya.'
Action: Search for two hardcover mystery picks in stock that can arrive before next weekend, send you the options and prices, and keep the card text ready.

How about: 'Happy birthday, Tom, thank you for being such a great person to work with. Hope you get a proper celebration.'
Action: Paste it into the card and sign it; I can shorten or warm it up if you want.

Sure, simple snacks for three kids. I don't know if Jun or his sister have any allergies or dislikes, so I'd like to check that first. I'll aim for easy things like fruit, crackers, cheese and something sweet.
Action: Build a PC Express cart for pickup tomorrow at 3:00 pm at your usual store, and send it to you to review before I check out, with a question about allergies.
